title: New Scholarships Will Help Foster Care Students Go to College
summary: Melania Trump on Saturday announced new scholarships for students at Louisiana State University who grew up in foster care. It is a team-up between LSU and her 'Fostering the Future' program. 'This achievement will give young people from foster care an anchor of stability, a strong educational foundation and a chance to build a wonderful life,' she said at an event with LSU President Wade Rousse. Trump and LSU raised more than $7 million in private gifts for the scholarships. MMR Group Inc., a company in Baton Rouge, gave $5 million, and other LSU Foundation donors gave more than $2 million. There are 14 students in the program at LSU and nine at Alabama, part of 100 students at 26 schools this semester. The first lady later went to the LSU-Alabama football game at Tiger Stadium, where players wore 'Be Best' patches. 'Fostering the Future' grew out of her 'Be Best' campaign from President Donald Trump's first term. She began working on foster care after that term ended in 2021.
why_it_matters: These scholarships can help kids who grew up in foster care go to college, just like other kids, and build the life they dream of.
